chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I become fully upright standing, then I do not know whether I performed rukuʿ or not?
He said: Yes, you have performed rukuʿ, so continue in your salat, for that is only from al-Shayṭān.

So this does not contradict what we mentioned, because the correct way regarding this report is that we interpret it as referring to one who has become fully upright standing from sajdah to the second rakʿah, or to the third after the first tashahhud, and then doubts the rukuʿ in the rakʿah whose ruling has already passed. He does not pay attention to that doubt, because he has already moved on to another state, and that doubt does not entail any ruling. And that which indicates this is...

key_terms.أَسْتَتِمُّ: I become complete or fully established in the posture
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony recited in the sitting of salat
key_terms.الشَّكِّ: doubt occurring about an act of salat
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانِ: the source of whisperings and baseless doubt

ai.seo_question: What should someone do in salat if they doubt having performed rukuʿ after already standing upright?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a person has already risen fully into the next standing position in salat and then doubts whether rukuʿ was performed, the prayer should continue without acting on the doubt. The accompanying explanation clarifies that this applies when the person has already moved beyond the earlier part of the rakʿah, so the doubt is disregarded as a passing insinuation from al-Shayṭān.
